title: When the House Burns
premise: Rosalind Quintana, a meticulous property surveyor who trusts ledgers more than people, is hired to appraise Hollowmere House before its sale—only to find the house cataloguing him back, its rooms rearranging to match his memories. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, Rosalind learns the founders built the house as a ritual of ownership: whoever holds the deed becomes both master and material. As the last resident, dying matriarch Edith Vane, prepares to sign the papers and pass the burden on, Rosalind must choose between fleeing with his found family—the crew and archivist who refuse to abandon him—or completing the founders' interrupted rite, which demands he surrender his documented self to the house's memory. In the end, he finishes the ritual not to claim power but to dissolve it, burning his own records inside the door so the house forgets how to own anyone; Hollowmere collapses into ash, and Rosalind walks out undocumented, finally free because nothing about him remains to be held.
about_author: Freya Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former land registry clerk from coastal Maine who spent eleven years cataloguing deeds to houses that no longer exist. Her fiction explores what buildings remember when their owners are gone.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He arrives at Hollowmere House to conduct a pre-sale appraisal, documenting every room with obsessive precision. The house is too clean, too symmetrical, and one closet measures larger outside than in. Emotional beat: quiet unease masked by professional competence.

chapters.title: Edith Vane Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He meets the last resident, Edith Vane, who refuses to sign preliminary papers until 'the survey is honest.' She warns him the house reads its visitors. That night his clipboard lists rooms he never entered. Beat: first crack in his rational worldview.

chapters.title: What the Crew Dug Up
chapters.summary: POV Tomas, excavation foreman. His crew strikes a stone lintel beneath the east lawn—a door, hinged inward, sealed from the inside with iron and wax. The ground around it is warm. Beat: dread entering through the physical world, not just Rosalind's head.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He researches the Vane family archive with junior archivist Priya Nair, discovering the founders' ledger: entries written in advance, describing events days before they occur—including tomorrow's entry naming him. Beat: his faith in records turns against him.

chapters.title: The Room That Wasn't Surveyed
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A hallway appears overnight containing furniture from his childhood home, down to the burn scar on the table. The house is building itself out of his memories. Beat: violation; the past weaponized.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. The crew pries at the buried door; scratch marks line its inner face, made by fingernails. One worker, Dez, begins sleepwalking toward the pit each night. Beat: the cost of curiosity made flesh.

chapters.title: The Founders' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Priya. She deciphers the ledger's structure: the house requires a resident to hold its memory, and each transfer of deed erases the previous holder from all records. Edith has no birth certificate, no photographs. Beat: horror reframed as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: An Offer of Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Edith offers him tea and truth: finish the founders' ritual and the house will keep him safe forever—owned, but never alone. For a man with no family, the offer lands like tenderness. Beat: temptation wearing the mask of found family.

chapters.title: Dez Goes In
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Dez breaks from the crew and opens the sealed door himself. Inside is a stairwell going up into soil. They pull him back changed—he now speaks in the founders' cadence and knows Rosalind's middle name. Beat: escalation, guilt.

chapters.title: The Appraisal Reverses
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. His survey documents begin writing themselves, appraising him: assets, liabilities, 'residual value.' The house has priced him. Beat: dehumanization via bureaucracy, his own language turned predatory.

chapters.title: Priya's Counter-Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Priya. She starts a second ledger recording the crew's real memories as armor against erasure, insisting that being remembered by someone is stronger than being recorded by something. Beat: hope; found family crystallizes as resistance.

chapters.title: What Edith Buried
chapters.summary: POV Edith (rare direct POV). Dying, she confesses she was meant to complete the ritual forty years ago and fled instead, leaving the house hungry and her sister inside the door. Beat: sympathy for the antagonist; generational guilt.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Edith signs the papers at last—but the signature transfers the holding to whoever completes the survey. Rosalind realizes his documentation has legally bound him to the house. Beat: trap sprung through his own thoroughness.

chapters.title: Night of the Open Door
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. The door stands open on the lawn though it was buried. Voices call each crew member by name. They barricade together in Priya's archive room, sharing stories aloud till dawn. Beat: terror answered by solidarity.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the founders' chapel-room he finds the rite's final page torn out—Edith took it. Without it, the ritual can't be finished or refused; the house will simply consume the current holder slowly. Beat: despair, stakes clarified.

chapters.title: Bargaining With Ash
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He confronts Edith; she trades the final page for his promise to free her sister rather than claim power. He understands the ritual was never about ownership—it was about feeding memory to the house. Beat: moral pivot.

chapters.title: Everything Documented Burns
chapters.summary: POV Priya. The house retaliates, devouring records—her counter-ledger pages blank themselves, Tomas's crew forgets his face. She rewrites the key names in blood-pricked ink that won't fade. Beat: sacrifice and defiance.

chapters.title: Down the Stairwell Going Up
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He enters the door with the final page, descending stairs that climb through strata of the house's swallowed lives. He finds Edith's sister, still cataloguing herself to stay whole. Beat: descent into the heart of memory.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At the threshold of completion, the house shows him everything he could be: kept, remembered, belonging. He recites the rite but substitutes dissolution for possession—offering his records instead of his self. Beat: climax; renunciation of power.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Forgets
chapters.summary: POV multiple, braided. The house ignites from within, un-burying itself to burn openly. Edith dies smiling, her sister's voice released. The crew drags a half-erased Rosalind onto the lawn as walls fold into embers. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Undocumented
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Weeks later, no record of his employment, appraisal, or visit exists—yet Priya's unfading ledger holds his name, handwritten. He keeps it not as prayer but as promise. Beat: quiet resolution; memory chosen over record.

chapters.title: A Door, Sealed From the Outside
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. The crew pours a new foundation over the ashes and seals a plain hatch—from the outside this time—with iron, wax, and all four of their names scratched above it. Not owners; witnesses. Beat: earned peace, vigilance, and love.
